posts.headline: Black Friday is on track for a record $12.9 billion online — but a record $21.3 billion of holiday shopping is going on Buy Now, Pay Later.
posts.source: Source: Adobe Analytics holiday forecast (2026); Deloitte Canada 2026 holiday outlook
posts.caption:
Black Friday is breaking records — and so is the borrowing behind it.

Adobe expects a record $12.9 billion in U.S. online sales today, part of a record $275.1 billion online holiday season (up 6.7% from last year's $257.8 billion).

Here's the part that follows you into January: a record $21.3 billion of that is going on Buy Now, Pay Later — the 'pay in 4' plans that split a purchase into four installments it's easy to lose track of.

North of the border it's the opposite mood: Canadians plan to spend about 5% less on gifts this year, Deloitte says.

My take: a deal you have to finance isn't really on sale. If a 'pay in 4' plan is the only way the cart fits, the cart is too full.

Would you put a Black Friday purchase on Buy Now, Pay Later? 👇

Source: Adobe Analytics holiday forecast (2026); Deloitte Canada 2026 holiday outlook
